q: How do map pins reference campaign records?
a: Pins carry record_kind and record_id; record text lives once whether accessed on map or in list.

q: How are campaign records hidden from players?
a: Quests, npcs, locations carry is_known flag; firestore.rules enforces read by members, write by DM.

q: What subcollections does a campaign document contain?
a: Sessions (number, title, play_date, summary, attendees), quests (title, description, state, level, npc_id, location_id), npcs (name, role, description, disposition, location, portrait, stat_block_id), locations (name, description, kind, map_id, marker_id).

q: How do detail layers control what appears at different map zoom levels?
a: Detail layers carry min_zoom and max_zoom; crossing a threshold replaces active layer with new layer image.

q: What is the status of Suno music integration?
a: Suno has no public API; generation is web-app only and developer API exploratory with curated partners only; listed as blocked in integration registry.

q: What pin icon types are available?
a: Twelve types: region, city, town, keep, dungeon, inn, temple, npc, quest, danger, treasure, note; npc, quest, treasure, danger take token layer color.

q: What are the upload size limits for postFile?
a: postFile enforces 10MB for user scope, 20MB for campaignMap and campaignAudio.

q: What is the Firestore access model?
a: User owns profile and data subtree; character is reachable by owner, viewers, editors, campaign DM, or public; campaign by DM and player_ids; chat by user; other access denied. Campaign page loads campaign and characters from Firestore with overview/party/maps and DM controls; maps store relative-coordinate markers with per-marker/per-map player visibility via onSnapshot.

q: How is the rules system implemented?
a: Rule systems are JSON documents; expression evaluator supports arithmetic, comparisons, ternaries, and math helpers without eval; calculation engine resolves in dependency order and throws RuleCycleError. 5e core is implemented; custom systems extend via extends field and merge by id to allow multi-system stacking.

q: How does the character sheet use the rules engine?
a: sheet.ts maps Character to engine by converting ability/skill titles to system ids and proficiency multipliers to tier ids, resolving modifiers once and recovering bonuses from stored totals; store.ts loads system stacks and derives on info/abilities/skills/savingThrows/special changes, reporting errors instead of throwing; components read $rules.resolved with fallback; RulePanels renders system-declared panels. Known issues: chat.ts fetches dead source.unsplash.com since 2024, Button/Field only cover login/signup, armour class/speed/initiative/hit point boxes two-way bound to stored values because engine-computed display changes player entry.

q: How is theme managed?
a: One theme list with one key. src/lib/dialogs/theme.ts owns availableThemes, getTheme, setTheme, keyed on dnd_theme.

q: Why don't login forms re-render?
a: Login and signup state is $state so inputs update.

q: What does the CI build require?
a: pnpm/action-setup, actions/setup-node@v6, and pnpm install --frozen-lockfile before build.

q: What does firebase.json serve?
a: dist with an SPA rewrite so client routing works. Previously served public which had no index.html.

q: What is the Firestore schema?
a: Snake_case throughout: replicate_api_key, display_name, photo_url, player_ids, character_ids, is_active. Character nests identity under info: character.info.name.

q: Why do characters overwrite each other?
a: getCharacterStore(id) now namespaces localStorage under ch_<id>_ so two characters no longer collide.

q: Which rule systems ship?
a: dnd5e.json is the core. nimble.json layers on damage reduction, mana, action budget, wounds, and progression-based hit point scaling. gunslinger.json adds Grit attribute, two skills, grit and misfire pools, and firearm derived values.

q: What scope variables exist in expressions?
a: level, prof, attr.<id>, mod.<id>, skill.<id>, save.<id>, sense.<id>, pool.<id>.max, derived.<id>, bonus.<id>, step.<key>. Missing bonus.* or step.* defaults to zero.

q: How does the rules system architecture work?
a: Systems are JSON under public/sources/systems/. src/lib/rules/expression.ts is a hand-written parser supporting arithmetic, comparisons, ternaries, and math helpers (floor, ceil, round, abs, sign, min, max, clamp, pow) with no eval(). src/lib/rules/system.ts resolves extends and merges by id so redefinitions replace. src/lib/rules/derive.ts resolves values in dependency order and throws RuleCycleError on cycles.

q: Can Replicate API features work on Firebase Hosting?
a: No. Calls target /replicate/... path which exists only as Vite dev proxy, not in production.

q: What setup is missing from the CI workflow?
a: pnpm install and pnpm/action-setup steps. Node modules and pnpm unavailable in job.

q: What are the bundle size issues?
a: index-*.js 589 kB and pdf-*.js 430 kB exceed 500 kB chunk limit.

q: Where does Firebase Hosting serve from in this project?
a: hosting.public is public/ per firebase.json. public/ contains only pdf.worker.min.js, sources/ and vite.svg, not the built application.

q: What does pnpm-workspace.yaml do?
a: pnpm 11 moved onlyBuiltDependencies from package.json. Holds build allowlist for @firebase/util and protobufjs.

q: What changed in TypeScript 7 for tsconfig?
a: baseUrl removed. paths now use ./src/... format.

q: Why must TypeScript be pinned to ^6.0.3?
a: svelte-check 4.7.6+ requires both TypeScript 6 and 7. svelte-check/bin/ts-version-check.js throws when major is 7. @typescript/native alias npm:typescript@^7.0.2 provides TS 7 compiler via --tsgo.

q: What is the project architecture?
a: Frontend-only static SPA built with Vite to dist/. Firebase, Octokit and Replicate are called from browser. Replicate proxy exists only as Vite dev-only in vite.config.ts.
